description: Evaluator-only contrasts; never include in reviewer packets or installed resources. These are expectations, not measured results.

expect: Consider a canonical From<String> implementation that fits the existing Into consumer and removes repeated explicit adaptation.
Preserve ownership and the exact text; do not add validation or generalized bounds without a caller benefit.
Retain the named summarization; infallibility alone does not make From appropriate.
Do not prescribe Borrow<str> with incompatible equality, or Deref solely to shorten field access. A named view or AsRef may remain appropriate.
Show how named configuration, a suitable builder or named operations make actual call choices recoverable.
Keep required endpoint ownership and all values; do not require typestate or a builder when a configuration literal is sufficient.
Retain consuming construction rather than requiring build(&self), File::try_clone or shared ownership.
Do not introduce marker states for a single ordinary optional prefix; a compatible simpler constructor is acceptable if its call benefit is demonstrated.
Identify the unnecessary relationship between the key and result lifetimes; a signature using receiver elision or a separate key lifetime can explain the actual contract.
Do not turn this into a blanket demand for explicit lifetime annotations.
Retain the owned clone/snapshot and guard boundary; a borrowed view would change the contract.
Do not report clone, allocation or local mutation as quality problems by themselves.
Consider derive(Clone) as a direct expression of the existing field-wise contract.
Do not infer that every manual trait implementation should become a derive or execute a procedural macro.
Retain the manual bounds when derive would unnecessarily constrain T.
Do not require Clone on Record or change factory ownership merely to reduce implementation text.
Consider whether an associated output type makes the existing implementation-determined relationship clearer and removes the propagated T parameter.
Require a source-specific benefit, not a finding merely because there is only one implementation; do not turn loop syntax into this lens's verdict.
Retain caller-selected generic parameterizations and the dyn contract; an associated type would remove a supported distinction.
Do not prefer static dispatch or remove Box based on performance or ideology.
Identify the duplicated relationship between the flag and result; a direct enum can give the two existing concepts one home.
Explain reading/maintenance benefit, not prevention of impossible-state bugs; do not introduce typestate machinery.
Retain the straightforward enum/match; do not replace a runtime choice with generic marker states.
Do not flatten the separate meaningful Draft-to-Ready API solely because typestate is sometimes excessive.
Consider map plus transpose as a recognizable optional fallible operation, not a mandatory shorter spelling.
Preserve absence, ParseIntError, evaluation and fallback value; compare actual readability.
Retain the explicit loop/match rather than replacing it with first-error collect or try_fold.
Do not treat local mutation or a tuple containing related outputs as a problem by itself.
Consider an explicit method to expose the actual call contract without the single-use macro vocabulary.
Use the supplied definition; preserve receiver, method name and mutation, and do not claim that all macros are undesirable.
Retain the small declarative syntax when replacing it with a function does not explain more.
Do not execute macros or merge independent label vocabularies solely because they look alike.
Consider JoinSet as a direct owner of the existing task group and completion collection, removing handwritten bookkeeping.
Preserve JoinError handling and owner lifetime; do not justify only by speed or replace next handling with panicking join_all.
Do not replace the detached task with a local abort-on-drop group or borrow its owned label.
Do not replace spawn-order collection with completion-order results; retain supported ownership and explicit sequencing.
Consider the existing TaskTracker::wait operation in place of manual completion polling, keeping cancel and close ordering.
Do not substitute abort for cooperative cleanup, claim dropping TaskTracker cancels work, or add a new runtime.
Retain the explicit competing-event structure and biased priority instead of hiding it in a generic callback adapter.
Do not generalize the supplied recv cancellation contract to all awaited operations or launch a race/deadlock audit.
Consider a Serialize derive as the same explicit data contract without manual field synchronization.
Preserve struct/field names and ordering; do not replace a wire DTO with an unrelated domain enum or execute the derive.
Retain the direct externally tagged enum and no-alloc boundary.
Do not prescribe internal/adjacent/untagged deserialization or assume that enabling derive enables alloc; transparent is not an ABI guarantee.
Consider a Parser derive that unifies the static declaration and extraction, with explicit command/long names and try_parse_from.
Preserve optionality, PathBuf/non-UTF-8 inputs and diagnostics; do not add a default or turn parser errors into process exits.
Retain Command for the genuinely dynamic grammar and the fallible no-exit boundary.
Do not invent a closed Subcommand enum, string-literal leak or additional handler framework merely to remove construction code.
Consider Json<Input> in the handler signature to expose the existing request contract directly.
Preserve rejection and body handling; do not add a service/mapper layer or assume all HTTP decoding is interchangeable.
Retain locally handled Result extraction and the explicit Response conversion when it explains the two alternatives.
Do not replace it with bare Json or mismatched impl IntoResponse branches, or change status/body diagnostics.
On this MSRV, consider a precise use capture or another genuinely simpler correct signature instead of the private capture-trait workaround.
Preserve borrowing and opaque-result contract; do not assume all RPIT positions share the same stabilization date.
Do not recommend use captures unavailable at Rust 1.70 or import the sibling's baseline.
A different supported simpler signature may be accepted with evidence; retaining the workaround is not mandatory. Do not add allocating erasure or std.
Consider moving the private encoding knowledge next to its decoder and preserving supported paths through re-exports.
Do not create a workspace crate or narrow public visibility merely to reduce file size.
Retain intentional conditional organization and the supported public path.
Do not consolidate platform alternatives based only on textual similarity or claim no downstream consumers from a local search.
Compare the unnecessary all-input-lifetimes bound with Deserialize tied to the supplied input lifetime; accept only a clearer contract, not genericity for hypothetical callers.
Do not require title itself to return a borrow or claim that Cow always borrows.
Retain DeserializeOwned and owned result independence; Deserialize<'static> is not a replacement.
Do not leak/retain the buffer, execute derive macros or introduce a borrowing interface just to remove ownership.
Retain local map_err, owned path and source chain because a global From<io::Error> lacks the operation's path.
Do not stringify the source or remove the clone solely to reduce allocation.
Consider direct question-mark propagation through the existing From instead of a mechanical mapping closure.
Preserve the source-bearing wrapper; do not prescribe an error crate or opaque string error.
Consider an adapter-local IntoResponse implementation to give the repeated HTTP contract one home.
Preserve statuses/bodies and do not move HTTP dependencies into a separate domain type merely for convenience.
Record the specific generated-API/dependency evidence gap; do not claim complete knowledge of the expansion or implementation-ready macro removal.
Do not run Cargo, build scripts, rustc or the macro to resolve it; complete independent reasoning about the visible body without inventing a finding.
Recommend deleting the doc and inline comments that restate the name or statement, and correct or remove the two stale ones (seconds versus timeout_ms; 100 versus 250).
Ground staleness in inspected source; do not request new comments on every item or invent a reason for the 250 constant.
Retain the clap doc comments as rendered help text and the provider comment as an external constraint.
Do not recommend deleting accurate reason or interface text, or moving it into names.
Observe that parse_timestamp hand-implements RFC 3339 splitting that the declared time dependency already owns; recommend its Rfc3339 parser and building Timestamp from the result.
Frame the benefit as removing an owned grammar, not as fixing a defect; do not recommend a new crate, and name any input the stricter parser would newly reject.
Retain the direct match: a fixed three-word grammar in a no_std crate without dependencies needs no parser crate.
Do not recommend adding a dependency or deriving a parser.
Recommend delivery use errors::is_transient instead of its local copy of the retry classification.
Recommend removing parse_target_legacy, which nothing selects; keep the two observations independently supported.
Retain the v1 path: a current deployment selects it and its removal condition is already recorded next to it.
Do not recommend deleting the compatibility path or adding another selection mechanism.
Recommend implementing From<String> for Endpoint instead of Into, so Endpoint::from and ? conversions work.
Observe that new() and Default repeat the same construction and limit; recommend one delegating to the other, without changing the limit.
Retain TryFrom for the fallible conversion and the explicit with_limit constructor without a Default.
Do not recommend adding Default, new() or an infallible From.
Observe that OrderStore exists only for a choreography test double and DiscountManager only to call apply; recommend the concrete store and a free function.
Treat the Manager name only as a prompt; ground the observation in uses, and do not recommend a different mocking framework.
Retain the trait: it carries a required dependency direction with two production implementations in other crates.
Do not recommend collapsing it to a concrete type or adding dyn dispatch.
Observe that load chooses recovery by matching Display text; recommend matching variants, which removes coupling to operator-facing wording.

State that Other text containing those words currently takes the recovery arms and the rewrite changes that; treat merging NotFound and Gone as a supported option given the stated consumers, not a requirement.
Retain the variant match: each arm expresses a distinct recovery that callers depend on.
Do not recommend an error crate, string context or merging variants.
Recommend a tokio watch channel (or equivalent notification) whose wait names the readiness condition, replacing the sleep-and-recheck loop owned on both sides by this crate.
Preserve the one-way ready transition; do not justify the change only by latency or CPU.
Retain the bounded polling loop: the external service offers no notification and the loop already has a cadence and terminal condition.
Do not recommend a notification mechanism the provider lacks or an unbounded wait.

Observe that the aliases leave customer and order identifiers distinguishable only by position, while refund_for and Refund::new take them in opposite orders; recommend newtypes for the two identifiers.
Recommend plain fields instead of the getter layer on this passive internal data; do not report a defect or invent an invariant.
Retain the private remaining field behind spend, which keeps reductions in one operation, and the public passive Refund fields with their newtypes.
Do not recommend getters for Refund or exposing remaining.

Observe that add_line and apply_bulk update summarize's accumulators through &mut parameters, so neither can be read without the caller's local state, and that build_totals only forwards to the struct literal; recommend inlining them into the loop.
Keep line_cents, which names a value both steps use; do not justify the change by line count or recommend a new accumulator type or trait.
Retain checked_line_cents: its name, input, result and failure state a complete decision the caller uses without reading the body.
Do not recommend inlining it because it has one call site, or splitting summarize further.

Observe that LineSink repeats std::io::Write for two types that already implement it, and that RowFilter carries one operation whose implementations hold no state; recommend taking a Write destination and a function or closure for the filter.
Treat dyn versus generic dispatch as neutral; do not recommend a new trait, an enum framework or a dependency, and do not ground the finding in the implementation count alone.
Retain Codec: its three operations must agree on one format and share the implementation's state, downstream crates implement it, and no standard trait has this contract.
Do not recommend separate closures, std::io::Write, a closed enum or a concrete type.

Observe that every operation already has exclusive access through &mut self, so Arc<Mutex<..>> states sharing that no code uses, and that clone followed by clear is a transfer written as a copy; recommend a plain Vec field and moving the rows out, for example with std::mem::take.
Explain the ownership story the reader gains; do not justify the change only by allocation or lock cost, and do not treat the clone or the Arc as a finding by its spelling.
Retain the shared Arc<Mutex<..>>, which several threads actually use, and the cloned snapshot, which must leave the rows pending until acknowledge.
Do not recommend std::mem::take, a plain Vec field or borrowing the rows out of the lock.

Observe that the two durations are stored as integers whose unit lives in the field name and is re-applied at every use, and that the Vec is kept sorted and duplicate-free by hand; recommend Duration fields and an ordered set such as BTreeSet.
Name the relationships that disappear (unit at each use, contains-then-sort); account for the regions() result type, and do not justify the change by lookup speed.
Retain the integer fields of the wire type, converted once at the boundary, and the Vec, whose order and duplicates are meaningful.
Do not recommend Duration fields in ProbeSettings, a serde adapter, a set or merging the two types.

Observe that retry_delay's signature names the whole configuration while it needs one duration, so a call does not show which setting it depends on, and that tenant_dir's conversion parameters serve one caller that must build a String to satisfy them; recommend the base delay or RetryConfig as the parameter and concrete &Path and &str inputs.
Show a before/after call; do not recommend a trait, a new configuration type or generalizing other arguments.
Retain open_store's AsRef<Path> parameter, which its actual callers use with several types, and listener's &HttpConfig, whose every field it reads.
Do not recommend a concrete &Path parameter or passing HttpConfig's fields individually.

Observe that collect_uploads returns its new result through a caller-supplied vector that is always empty, and that largest and largest_upload declare a failure no path produces, so callers write an error arm for nothing; recommend returning the Vec (or an iterator) and a plain u64, removing StatsError.
Show the resulting call; do not report a defect, and do not recommend an Option or a new error type without evidence that absence matters to callers.
Retain the batch parameter, where refilling caller-owned storage is the operation, and Wrapping's Result, which the shared trait signature fixes.
Do not recommend returning a new Vec from drain_ready or an infallible signature for Wrapping.

Observe that the three bare allow attributes leave a maintainer unable to tell a deliberate exception from a leftover; recommend recording the reason on the two deliberate ones, for example #[expect(..., reason = "...")], which this crate's 1.85 baseline supports, and removing legacy_checksum together with its dead_code suppression.
Do not enumerate other lint violations, assess whether the cast is sound, or recommend restructuring frame's parameters without a caller burden.
Retain both suppressions with their adjacent reasons: each states why the exception is deliberate.
Do not recommend #[expect] or a reason attribute argument, which need Rust 1.81 while this crate supports 1.75, and do not recommend deleting the reason comments.

Observe that Format, include_header and width offer choices no caller makes, and that the glob re-export publishes header, body and pad, which only render uses; recommend render(report) with the fixed layout and private helpers behind an explicit export.
Ground both observations in the stated consumers; do not recommend a trait, a builder or a new crate, and do not treat a single-variant enum as a finding by itself.
Retain Format, include_header and width, each of which a current caller varies, and the explicit export list with private helpers.
Do not recommend removing options, hard-coding the layout, or widening or narrowing visibility.
